entities.summary:
Pope Lucius II, born Gherardo Caccianemici dal Orso, was head of the Catholic Church and ruler of the Papal States from March 9, 1144, to his death in February 22, 1145. His pontificate was marked by the unrest in Rome associated with the Commune of Rome and its attempts to wrest control of the city from the papacy.

He supported Empress Matilda's claim to the Kingdom of England during the Anarchy and had a tense relationship with King Roger II of Sicily. Lucius II played a significant role in shaping the political landscape of medieval Italy, particularly in the context of the Papal States' struggles for power and influence.

The legacy of Pope Lucius II can be seen in the continued tensions between the papacy and city-states, as well as his support for Empress Matilda's claim to the English throne. He left a lasting impact on the Catholic Church and the history of medieval Europe.

In 2019, a team of archaeologists discovered a previously unknown tomb beneath St. Peter's Basilica, believed to be the final resting place of Pope Lucius II.
